verdict.reasoning: Headache for ~3 days, worsening, constant with fluctuations and rated 8/10: “around three days ago…”, “it kind of comes and goes… it is there all the time, but like sometimes it's stronger”, and “Ohh it's probably a eight.”
Patient describes pain as all over but worse around right eye: “it kind of feels all over my head, but like mainly, um, around my right eye.”
Dull with intermittent sharp pain and gradual onset: “it's kind of, it's dull but sometimes it gets a bit sharper. So basically it like, it developed gradually, I guess.”

Photopsia, photophobia, nausea (feeling sick), and difficulty focusing are all reported: “I got this like weird shooting lights…”, “now like light is quite annoying, my eyes… it hurts to look at bright lights”, “I… I’m sick with the headache. But I, no vomiting.” and “it's hard to focus though.”

Patient denies these symptoms: “Not loss of vision, I wouldn't say”, “have you had any loss of vision or blurry vision? [implied no]”, “Any neck pain or neck stiffness?… No.”, “any difficulty with speaking…? No.”, “Any difficulty… with weakness in your arms and legs? Patient: No”, “Any temperatures, or fevers? Patient: No.”, “Any rashes at all…? Patient: …no”, and “any recent head injuries at all? Patient: Uh, no.”

She mentions computer work and mild stress but does not clearly identify them as triggers: “I work in IT… difficult to focus… reduce the brightness of my screen” and “it's been a bit stressful… but… nothing out of the ordinary.” The statement that these are possible triggers is an inference not stated by patient or doctor.

No chronic conditions and no prior migraine diagnosis: “Are you otherwise fit and well… do you have any other medical history? Patient: Yeah, I think so. It's just the headache.” and “Any history of migraines at all? Patient: Not myself, I've never had a migraine.”
Migraine family history: “my sister and my mom have them quite frequently.” and “my mom's is like quite bad… usually when there's like a season changing… Takes her out for a few days.”
Ibuprofen details: “I tried uh Ibuprofen… I took, like a few. Um for the last two days” and later “How many tablets did you take of Ibuprofen? Patient: Uh, three a day.” and “it doesn't really help.”
No known drug allergies: “Do you have any allergies to any medications? Patient: Mm not that I know of.”
Living situation and work: “I live with housemates. So, three of them. So we're four” and “I work in IT. So I work with computers a lot.”
Glasses and no recent eye test: “Do you wear glasses? Patient: Yes, I do.” and “Have you had any recent eye check…? Patient: No, uh I've been wearing them since I was five… it's quite a long time.”
Social smoking and drinking: “I socially smoke. And I drink only socially.”

Doctor assesses likely migraine: “I… unfortunately I do think this could be, a headache very similar to a migraine… the history is very suggestive of it… it may just be a one-off.” While the exact phrasing “without aura versus probable migraine with visual phenomenon” is interpretive, it reflects the doctor’s stated diagnostic impression and the described visual symptoms.

Doctor discusses dose frequency and option of naproxen but not specific mg: “You can take up to two tablets, three times a day… Or, I can prescribe you something stronger, like Naproxen.” The fact adds a specific 400 mg q6–8h regimen that is not mentioned.
Doctor proposes paracetamol and codeine as add-ons: “we can also add in other, painkillers like, Paracetamol, or Codeine. Which might be helpful as well.”
There is no discussion of limiting acute medications to 2–3 days per week or medication overuse headache in the transcript.

Hydration, regular meals, sleep hygiene, and resting in a dark room are not advised in the transcript. Only screen brightness is mentioned by the patient, not as doctor advice: “I had to like reduce the uh, brightness of my screen.”

Doctor advises a headache diary but without specified contents: “It may be worth keeping a headache diary so we can try and work out what's… if there's any triggers…”. The fact adds specific fields (onset, duration, severity, medications, menses) that are not mentioned.

Follow-up timing and earlier review if worsening: “I'd like you to come back and see me, in about uh, a week's time, week to two weeks' time.” and “if your headaches aren't getting any better, or they're getting worse… give me a call, or come back and see me sooner.”

Prophylaxis discussion plan: “If you are having more frequent episodes of these type of headaches. We can think about giving you medications as, prophylactic… But we can have that discussion next time.”

Safety-net advice is narrower in transcript: “if you're having any problems with your vision, or weakness in your arms and legs, or you're just not feeling very well. Just give me a call, and come back and see me.” The fact adds urgent care triggers (severe headache, persistent vomiting, fever/neck stiffness, head injury) that are not stated.
